newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: STRAITS NEARS DECISION ON WHIM CREEK COPPER.
newsitem.headline: STRAITS NEARS DECISION ON WHIM CREEK COPPER.

text.p: Straits Resources Ltd said on Tuesday it planned very shortly to make a development decision on its Whim Creek copper project, which could be operating as early as April next year.
Straits managing director Brian Rear said the proposed 10,000 tonne a year mine in Western Australia was fully engineered, and would take 34 weeks to develop once a decision was made.
Whim Creek would have a project cost of 57 cents a pound, against 40 cents a pound at Straits' 60 percent owned Girilambone copper mine in New South Wales, he said.
However, this was still at the lower end of the cost curve.
"The general feeling is that if we can get around 60 cents a pound ... then we are fairly competitive," Rear told a Bell Securities Ltd base metals conference here.
Straits last month moved to full control of the project, paying A$5.5-A$7.5 million, depending on copper prices, for the 40 percent holding of Dominion Mining Ltd.
Capital costs for the project have been estimated at A$18 million.
Rear said Straits was also carrying out a pre-feasibility study at its half-owned Maroochydore project in Western Australia, with most work on metallurgical testing.
The project was forecast to produce copper at 40 cents a pound, he said.
At the Sebuku coal project in Kalimantan, Indonesia, Straits had already contracted 85 percent of the 1998 production to buyers in Japan, Hong Kong, Thailand and Indonesia, Rear said.
The coal was being sold for around US$26-27 a tonne, he said, compared with estimated production costs of about US$17 a tonne.
Sebuku is planned to produce 1.35 million tonnes a year for 11 years, with the first shipment of coal planned for end-1997.
Straits share were trading down one cent at A$2.12 at 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT).
